screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows the Earth's tectonic plates, drawn on a globe that can be turned or on a flat map. Layers of real data can be drawn on top of it: plate boundaries coloured by type, plate motion arrows, earthquake epicentres, volcanoes and hotspots, shaded relief of the land surface and sea floor, and isochrons of the ocean floor — lines of equal crustal age, which run parallel to the spreading ridges and get older away from them.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a switch between the globe and the flat map, a checkbox for each data layer, an earthquake depth filter, controls that run plate motion forwards and backwards through geological time, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Switch on a pair of layers and look for where they line up — earthquakes and volcanoes around the Pacific, or ridges and shallow earthquakes down the middle of the Atlantic.

viewDetails.global: The flat map is showing. It can be moved east and west, and zoomed in to look at one region closely.
viewDetails.globe: The Earth is showing as a globe, which can be turned to bring any part of it into view.

depthDetails.all: Earthquakes of all depths are shown.
depthDetails.shallow: Only shallow earthquakes, less than 70 kilometres deep, are shown.
depthDetails.intermediate: Only intermediate-depth earthquakes, 70 to 300 kilometres deep, are shown.
depthDetails.deep: Only deep earthquakes, more than 300 kilometres deep, are shown.

timeDetails.present: Plates are in their present-day positions.
timeDetails.past: Plates are shown as they were about {{value}} million years ago.
timeDetails.future: Plates are shown as they would be about {{value}} million years from now.

controls.viewSwitchHelp: Draw the Earth as a globe that can be turned, or as a flat rectangular map.
controls.globeHelp: Drag the globe to turn the Earth. With the globe focused, the left and right arrow keys move the view east and west, and the up and down arrow keys move it north and south.
controls.mapHelp: Drag the map to move it. With the map focused, the left and right arrow keys move the view east and west; once the map is zoomed in, the up and down arrow keys move it north and south.
controls.zoomHelp: Zoom in to look at one region closely, or out to bring the whole world back.
controls.depthFilterHelp: Show earthquakes of every depth, or only one depth band.
controls.timeSliderHelp: Move plates back into the past or forward into the future, in millions of years.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a cross-section through three blocks of crust floating in the mantle: fixed oceanic crust on the left, fixed continental crust on the right, and in the middle a block whose temperature, composition and thickness you control. Each block settles to the height at which it floats.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has three sliders for the middle block, a choice of whether to colour the rock by density, by temperature or by both, a choice between a three-dimensional block and a flat section with a vertical-exaggeration slider, a zoom control, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Make the middle block thicker and watch it rise, then make it denser and watch it sink — and notice that it sinks deeper into the mantle at the same time as its surface drops.

crust.crustDetails: The middle block is {{thickness}} km thick with a density of {{density}} kilograms per cubic metre.
crust.elevationAbove: Its surface stands {{value}} km above sea level.
crust.elevationBelow: Its surface lies {{value}} km below sea level.
crust.zoomDetails: The view reaches down to the {{extent}}.

controls.temperatureSliderHelp: Warm the middle block. Hot rock expands, so it becomes slightly less dense and floats a little higher.
controls.compositionSliderHelp: Move the middle block between iron-rich rock and silica-rich rock. Iron-rich rock is denser and floats lower.
controls.thicknessSliderHelp: Set how thick the middle block is, from 4 to 70 kilometres. A thicker block floats higher and reaches deeper.
controls.colorModeHelp: Colour the cross-section by density, by temperature, or by both at once.
controls.zoomHelp: Pull back from the crust to the lithosphere, or to the whole Earth including the mantle and core.
controls.probeHelp: Move the probe through the cross-section to read the temperature and density where it sits.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a cross-section through the boundary between two tectonic plates. Until plates are chosen it is empty, with a drop zone on each side. Once both sides have a plate and a boundary type has been chosen, the clock runs and the boundary evolves — a slab descending, an ocean opening, or mountains rising.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has three crust pieces to place in the drop zones, a choice between automatic and manual motion, a boundary type chooser, play, pause and step controls with a speed slider, Rewind and New Crust buttons, a choice of what colours the rock, a choice between a three-dimensional block and a flat section with a vertical-exaggeration slider, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Put old oceanic crust against a continent and converge them, and watch where the volcanoes appear relative to the trench.

plateMotion.platesOne: One drop zone has a plate; the other is empty.
plateMotion.platesBoth: {{left}} crust on the left, {{right}} crust on the right.
plateMotion.motionNone: No boundary type has been chosen yet.
plateMotion.motionSubduction: They are converging, and the {{side}} plate is subducting beneath the other.
plateMotion.motionCollision: They are converging, and neither can subduct, so the crust is thickening into mountains.
plateMotion.motionRifting: They are diverging, and new ocean floor is forming between them.
plateMotion.timeFinished: The boundary has run its full {{value}} million years.

controls.crustPieceHelp: Press to pick this crust up, then press a drop zone to place it on that side. It can also be dragged straight into a zone.
controls.boundaryTypeHelp: Choose whether the two plates converge or diverge. Only the boundaries these two plates can actually make are available.
controls.rewindHelp: Run the same two plates from the beginning again.
controls.newCrustHelp: Clear both plates and start over.
controls.speedHelp: How many million years pass per second.
controls.colorModeHelp: Colour the cross-section by density, by temperature, or by both at once.
controls.probeHelp: Move the probe through the cross-section to read the temperature and density where it sits.
controls.motionModeHelp: In automatic mode the clock runs on its own once a boundary type is chosen. In manual mode you pull the plates yourself and time advances only while you do.
controls.handleHelp: Drag a handle away from the boundary to pull the plates apart, or towards it to push them together. Arrow keys advance and retreat the clock.
controls.leftDropZoneHelp: Press to place the crust you have picked up on the left, or to clear the plate already there.
controls.rightDropZoneHelp: Press to place the crust you have picked up on the right, or to clear the plate already there.

plateMotion.modeAutomatic: The clock runs on its own.
plateMotion.modeManual: Time advances only while a plate handle is moved.

screenSummary.playArea: The play area shows a globe carrying a published reconstruction of the Earth's plates over the last 250 million years. The continents move continuously as the clock runs, while the plates and the boundaries between them are rebuilt every five million years, because plates themselves are born and destroyed as oceans open and close.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a checkbox for each layer, a slider and play controls that run the reconstruction from the present day back to 250 million years ago, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Run the clock back and watch the Atlantic close: by 250 million years ago every continent has gathered into Pangaea.

timeDetails.present: The globe shows the Earth as it is today.
timeDetails.past: The globe shows the Earth as it was about {{value}} million years ago.

controls.globeHelp: Drag the globe to turn the Earth. With the globe focused, the left and right arrow keys move the view east and west, and the up and down arrow keys move it north and south.
controls.timeSliderHelp: Move the slider to choose an age, from the present day back to 250 million years ago.
controls.coastlines: Show the continents, carried by the plates they sit on.
controls.plates: Show the tectonic plates that existed at this age.
controls.boundaries: Show plate boundaries, coloured by type.
controls.deforming: Show the belts where the model treats the lithosphere as deforming rather than rigid.

blockView.sectionViewHelp: Choose between a flat cross-section and a three-dimensional block of Earth with the section cut across its front face.
blockView.verticalExaggerationHelp: Stretch the block vertically. At one times, depths and distances across the block are drawn at the same scale.
blockView.rulerHelp: Drag the ruler onto the cross-section to measure how thick a layer is or how deep something lies. Use the arrow keys to move it.
blockView.viewBlock: The section is drawn as a three-dimensional block of Earth at {{exaggeration}}.
